_meta.confidenceKey: high = confirmed on an official or primary source; medium = consistent sources but no independent primary confirmation; low = plausible guess / weak match. 'confidence' on members = how sure we are WHICH organisation the acronym means; 'membership*' fields = whether Local Host's membership is verified.
_meta.rule: Only items with membershipVerified=true / confidence high may be shown on the site without owner confirmation.

members.description: Government agency (legal entity of public law under the Ministry of Economy and Sustainable Development of Georgia) that shapes and implements state tourism policy and promotes Georgia abroad.

members.description: GNTA's MICE (meetings, incentives, conferences, exhibitions) unit, which promotes Georgia as a business-events destination and works with member hotels, venues and DMCs/PCOs.

An ITB Berlin 2023 release says GCEB was set up in 2016 as a member-based organisation, and 44 members were reported in May 2018 (https://strategeast.org/?p=15309). It fits Local Host's MICE profile, but Local Host is NOT in the bureau's current DMC & PCO directory (re-checked 2026-10-10: all 33 company slugs over 6 pages). Fresh searches for 'CEBG' with Georgia, Tbilisi or tourism found no other organisation using that acronym. The owner must confirm what CEBG stands for and whether the membership is current.

awardProgramme.name: Welcome to Georgia! National Tourism Awards (now also branded 'National Tourism Awards of Georgia' / NTA)
awardProgramme.organiser: Welcome to Georgia! National Tourism Awards project (private). GNTA co-organised it on behalf of the Ministry of Economy and Sustainable Development in 2015–2017 (it was in its 'third year' as co-organiser in 2017). In 2016 the winners were decided by professional jury scores plus an online vote, with BDO Georgia as independent auditor. For the 2026 edition, GNTA appears among the partner logos and the evaluation (expert jury, cross-industry assessment and public vote) is 'led and conducted by Grant Thornton'. Companies enter by registering themselves: in 2016 via the awards website, and in 2026 for a fee of 500 GEL per category. In this programme, 'nominee' therefore means a registered entrant, not a shortlisted finalist.

travelife.wording: Local Host is a Travelife Partner — independently assessed against the Travelife Partner criteria for tour operators and travel agents (recognised since November 2025).
travelife.badge: Travelife PARTNER logo only (from the Travelife toolkit / Communication Guidelines supplied to the company), linked to the public register. Never the 'Travelife Certified' logo.
travelife.notes: Public Travelife register lists 'Local Host LLC', Georgia, level Partner (level_id 3), first approval 2025-11-26, valid until 2027-11-26. Re-checked 2026-10-10: unchanged. Travelife has two recognition levels. Partner is the entry level: about 60 mandatory criteria, an independent desk-based assessment of the sustainability management system, and reassessment every 2 years. Certified is the highest level: 200+ criteria and an extensive on-site audit. 'Engaged' is the preparatory phase and gives no right to use a recognition logo. The company's Nov 2025 Sustainability Report (Travelife format) still shows many Certified-level criteria with target dates in 2026–2027, which is consistent with Partner status. EU Directive 2024/825 (EmpCo) has applied since 27 Sept 2026 (European Commission; transposition deadline 27 Mar 2026). It tightens green claims and labels for EU consumers, so keep claims specific and tied to the Travelife assessment. Georgian peers on the register (re-checked): VisitGeorgia and Georgian DMC are Certified (2026-01-18 to 2028-01-18); Promethea Voyages is a Partner (2025-02-11 to 2027-02-11).

hosts.name: Sisatura — Marika & Enry
hosts.place: Sisatura (Sisa Tura) ethno-village, Chkhoria village, Zugdidi municipality
facts: Family-hosted Megrelian ethnographic village in Chkhoria, about 11 km from Zugdidi on the road to Mestia.
Covers about 3 hectares: traditional Megrelian houses and household artefacts, an artificial lake, an old water mill and a small farm with animals.
Offers Megrelian cooking classes and tastings (e.g. ghomi, elarji, gebzhalia), folklore and a traditional supra with a tamada.
The hosts greet arriving guests; georgia.travel says with Dirfa, a Megrelian fruit vodka. Local Host's policy describes it as 'at the gate of Sisatura with a shot of Chacha and a big smile'.
Welcoming guests since 2019; visits by booking (GNTA listing).
hosts.note: The GNTA listing names the hosting family as the Chitanava family. Second host's name is spelled 'Ermine'/'Henry' in the policy and 'Enry' in the template — owner to confirm spelling.
